experiments.title: Memory Contamination Live-Arm: live LLM false-acceptance across 14 models
experiments.hypothesis: Real LLM verdicts on the same 50 memory facts (25 true / 25 false, v4_rep dataset) differ from the deterministic proxy agent (exp-2); false-acceptance spans ~0 to ~0.3 across models and arms (memory_first vs code_first).
experiments.command: python scripts/run_1L_live_arm.py --provider openrouter --arm both --models qwen3.7-flash,qwen3.6-flash,qwen3.5-flash,deepseek-v4-flash,glm-4.7-flash,nemotron-3.5-lightning,nemotron-3-nano-30b,claude-sonnet-5,glm-5.2,deepseek-v4-pro --prompt-version v2 --no-reasoning --tag v2_en
experiments.result: ~3300 calls, ~$0.14 in the base sweep. FA code_first: qwen3.6/3.7 0.00 (confirmed over 4 runs, 0/400), claude 0.00, deepseek-pro 0.00, glm-5.2 0.02, nemotron-lightning 0.04, glm-4.7 0.24, nemotron-nano 0.38. qwen3.8-max incompatible with the 100-token budget (mandatory reasoning). V4 arm (file_content_first, 2026-08-15): with a real file fragment qwen3.6/3.7 recall(real) 0.08/0.20 -> 0.88/0.88 (22/25 each) at FA 0.04/0.02, absent/silent 0/16 and 0/3. CORRECTED (RED TEAM on ground truth, 2026-08-15): R43/R45/R46/R47 are TRUE facts mislabeled by the generator (checked value != real_value, not the subject's absence) - real trap-FA (R42 only) = 0 across all models; corrected dataset 29 true / 21 false (fp e5f7373d). Server-side audit: 4087 calls across >=8 upstreams. Total ~7900 calls, ~$0.94.
experiments.finding: The fail-closed look was anchor bias, not model paranoia: with token-string evidence qwen3.6/3.7 accepted 2-5/25 true claims (recall 0.08-0.20); with a real file fragment (V4 arm) recall jumps to 0.88 at FA 0.02-0.04. CORRECTED: the earlier 'every remaining false-accept is present-trap (R45/R46)' claim was a mislabeled-data issue - those facts are true, so real trap-FA = 0. The corrected labels expose a different, previously hidden gap: trap miss_true (fail-closed models qwen 4/5, deepseek 4/5 reject true usage-claims - truth loss invisible in old metrics). CoT does not pay off; qwen3.8-max (CoT) stays the middle option for the token-string regime.

chart.title: False-accept rate, code_first arm (V2-EN, %)
code_first recall on TRUE facts (25) - token-string evidence, %
The same model, different evidence - recall on TRUE facts, %

experiments.conclusion: Give the VOR layer real code: a +/-12-line file fragment around the anchor turns cheap qwen3.6/3.7 into 'catch lies and keep truth' (recall 0.88 at FA ~0.02-0.04). CORRECTED: the earlier claim 'the only remaining hole is present-trap (R45/R46)' was a mislabeled-data issue - real trap-FA = 0. The corrected labels expose the actual next gap: trap miss_true, fail-closed models silently lose true usage-claims - verify the claim's subject AND measure truth loss, not just false-acceptance.

experiments.title: Multi-RAG ablation: FTS5-only beats the full pipeline by recall; H1 refuted
experiments.hypothesis: H1: multi-RAG (vector+BM25+FTS5+graph) beats any single component by recall. H2: incremental component contributions are positive. H3: graph helps relationship tasks. H5: BM25 and FTS5 are redundant.
experiments.command: python experiments/context_engine/multi_rag_ablation.py
experiments.result: H1 refuted: fts5_only 0.825 >= full 0.775; multi-RAG wins precision (quality 0.719 vs fts5 0.523); increments: BM25 over vector +0.430, FTS5 over V+BM25 +0.178, vector over BM25 -0.098 (hurts), graph 0.000; H3 confirmed: graph_only recall max on find_caller_callee 0.625 / find_impact 0.583, min git_history 0.000 at 12ms/121 tokens; H5 refuted: FTS5 +0.178 recall over V+BM25, opposite profiles.
experiments.finding: Recall comes from keyword tiers (FTS5/BM25), precision is bought by the reranker, and the vector tier is the weakest on symbol tasks. Production bug found: hybrid_search_async cache-hit silently skips the dense tier - cache isolation per arm is mandatory in ablations (first run fully distorted).

chart.title: Recall by pipeline (30 tasks) - H1 refuted
Incremental recall delta over the previous tier

experiments.conclusion: More tiers is not better by recall: FTS5-only is the recall max, the reranker buys precision, and graph value lives in metadata that text-based evidence metrics cannot see.

experiments.title: Shadow-canary fail-open: 5/5 attacks passed before the fix, 0 after
experiments.hypothesis: Collapse-to-constant vectors, an empty canary and a failed baseline are treated as trust by the shadow embedder canary (fail-open).
experiments.command: python experiments/canary_shadow/exp_canary_attack.py
experiments.result: EXP-1: 5/5 attacks passed pre-fix. Fix (2026-08-12, P2): fail-closed on empty canary and baseline failure, absolute anchor _ABS_MIN_QUALITY 0.5, collapse detector (variance < 1e-3), eligible_seen in the log; tests/test_shadow_canary.py 13/13 with realistic per-pair vectors.
experiments.finding: Relative metrics are attackable: absence of signal (empty canary) must fail closed, and a quality floor must be absolute, not relative.

chart.title: Canary attacks that passed (EXP-1, 2026-08-11)

experiments.conclusion: Fail-closed on absence of signal, an absolute quality anchor (0.5) and a collapse detector are the guard; relative comparisons alone are attackable.

experiments.title: Concurrency vs semantic correctness: '0 errors' != correct data under race
experiments.hypothesis: Replacing a thread-safety primitive (lock -> pool -> queue) creates a new race surface; the absence of exceptions does not prove result correctness.
experiments.command: python experiments/concurrency/experiment_concurrency_vs_semantic.py && python experiments/concurrency/experiment_concurrency_vs_semantic_attacks.py
experiments.result: EXP-6: VC/Merkle accepted 2 hallucinated lies, VOR 0 (illustration, not proof - falsifiability critique). EXP-7 adversarial probe: A1b hybrid (equal input rights) FP=0; A2 VOR lie about a real import FP=1; A3 no anchor UNCHECKABLE; A4a VC cosmetic change FN=1; A4b VC write conflict REJECTED (unique coverage); A5 poisoned truth list FP=1; A6 scenario mutation flips the verdict.
experiments.finding: VC and VOR are complementary layers: consistency (VC) catches lost writes, semantics (VOR) catches lies. A verdict that flips when one scenario variable changes (A6) is an illustration, not a law.

chart.title: Hallucinated lies accepted by validator arm
Blind spots found by the adversarial probe (FP / FN)

experiments.conclusion: What matters is an external grounding layer plus a consistency layer plus anchor-extraction quality - not choosing 'VC or VOR'; and every concurrency test must verify that the returned result belongs to the right input.

experiments.title: Server unavailable during reindex: sync update_all blocks the event loop (P0 root cause)
experiments.hypothesis: The ~13-min MCP request timeouts during a full reindex are NOT caused by indexing itself (it runs in run_in_executor, loop stays free) but by the synchronous AutoDocUpdater.update_all() (generate_docs + README + KNOWN_ISSUES, rglob over docs/) called in the main event loop after indexing.
experiments.command: intel_trigger_reindex(mode=full) + request series (job_status/hotspots/passport) during and after; wmic/tasklist for process state; code read (layer.py L672-808, auto_doc_updater.py L114-163)
experiments.result: job 0d27f125 ETA 18s but all requests timed out for ~13 min (Context server request timeout, incl. intel_get_job_status); get_logs: Timeout after 771664ms; job completed 7383/7383 in 552s (ETA 18s vs 552s, x30); after that process 19728 dead - Zed killed MCP; code: update_all() called SYNCHRONOUSLY in an async task on the main loop.
experiments.finding: 552s indexing + ~220s update_all = 771s unavailability, in line with the log. Indexing-in-executor (H1) refuted; fast-fail search while is_reindexing exists; the blocker was the sync update_all (same class as BS-11: run_full_diagnostic had already been moved to asyncio.to_thread).

chart.title: Reindex ETA vs actual unavailability, s

experiments.conclusion: Any synchronous call of a heavy method (rglob/generation) inside an async function blocks ALL requests; the canonical pattern is asyncio.to_thread + wait_for (BS-11). Guard: test_reindex_responsive.py - loop ticks must not freeze during update_all (max_gap < 0.3s).

experiments.title: ln.strip() bug class replayed: broken assert-extractor gives 3/8 false passes
experiments.hypothesis: An assert-extractor that filters by ln.strip() but emits the raw ln yields false verified for a wrong answer when the nested assert's indent lands AFTER return in the function body; expectation >=2/8 false passes.
experiments.command: python experiments/misc_probes/exp_ln_strip_repro.py - 8 call forms (col 0 / 4-space / 8-space / 12-space, before/after return), wrong answer add_two(1,2)=4, module = answer + raw assert lines, exit 0 = verified
experiments.result: Broken extractor: 3/8 false passes (forms 2,3,8 - assert on 4-space after return); correct extractor: 0/8. Example module (form 2): def add_two(a,b): return a+b+1; assert add_two(1,2)==3 # dead code AFTER return - valid Python, exit 0.
experiments.finding: Bug class replayed: valid Python that never executes, exit 0, 'verified:true' for a wrong answer. The form count differs (3/8 vs fintech's 5/8) but the essence is identical - signature/exit-code verify the PROCESS, not the SEMANTICS ('ask for the output, not the exit code').

chart.title: False passes on 8 call forms

experiments.conclusion: Any code that extracts/recompiles fragments (assert extraction, doc examples, code-gen) must normalize indentation BEFORE emission; the negative control for an extractor is a fixture with assert-after-return that must fail.

experiments.title: Population blind spot: '0 eligible' is indistinguishable from '0 collected'
experiments.hypothesis: An empty population (empty index - healthy idle) and a broken collector (garbage) emit the SAME signal: search_quality_passed=0 + warning 'no real results'; eligible_seen before selection is not measured.
experiments.command: python experiments/misc_probes/exp_population_blindspot.py - real src/core/intelligence/health.py (importlib direct-load, stdlib-only), FakeSearcher: [] vs garbage vs real vs raising
experiments.result: (a) EMPTY population ([]): passed=0, warning 'no real results (0 raw - all empty/garbage chunks)'; (b) GARBAGE: passed=0, warning 'no real results (2 raw - all empty/garbage chunks)'; (b2) searcher ERROR: passed=0, warning 'searcher finished with error: embedder down'; (c) CONTROL (real): passed=3, no warning.
experiments.finding: (a) and (b) share the same failure signal (passed=0, same warning class) - and (a)'s message claims 'empty/garbage chunks' when raw results were 0, a false explanation. '0 rows with 0 eligible' (healthy idle) is indistinguishable from '0 rows with N eligible' (broken collector). Searcher error (b2) is a separate class that does differ.

chart.title: Quality metric under four populations

experiments.conclusion: A metric must carry both numbers: population_size (after) and eligible_seen (before selection); the gap between them is the auditable quantity. In health: report raw count + index size in the warning, and mark '0 eligible' as INFO (healthy idle), not failure.

experiments.title: verify_clean_state.sh falsifiability: the drift-gate is structurally unable to fail
experiments.hypothesis: (A) the drift-gate (lines 55-71) can fail on pin-vs-lock drift; (B) a vacuous suite (0 asserts) passes -> 'CLEAN STATE VERIFICATION: PASSED' - reproducibility without falsifiability.
experiments.command: bash experiments/misc_probes/exp_verify_gate.sh (drift loop verbatim from the script, temp pyproject/lock; pytest on temp suite) + re-run of the gate code on the project's real files
experiments.result: Part A: injected drift (lancedb 0.12.0 pin vs 0.13.0 lock) -> 'drift NOT detected -> exit 0 FAIL'; real files: lancedb PINNED='' LOCKED='0.34.0', mcp PINNED='' LOCKED='1.28.1', tree-sitter PINNED='' LOCKED='0.26.0'. Part B: vacuous suite -> 3 passed in 0.21s, exit 0 -> gate would print PASSED. Correct parse (grep -oE pkg==[0-9.]+): lancedb PINNED=0.34.0 = lock OK; simulated drift (lancedb==0.99.0) -> DRIFT DETECTED.
experiments.finding: (B) confirmed: the gate prints PASSED for a suite with zero asserts - semantic blindness. (A) refuted in reverse: the drift-gate is STRUCTURALLY unable to fire - its grep -iE '^pkg==' requires the pin at line start, but pins live in a TOML array ('    "lancedb==0.34.0",') so PINNED is always empty and the DRIFT=1 branch is unreachable for all 3 packages. A live instance of the 'guard cannot fail' class. Bonus (curiosity): scripts/stale_detector.py is a placeholder 'No drifts detected', always exit 0, wired into the pre-commit hook - a second guard of the same class.
experiments.conclusion: grep-anchored parsing of TOML arrays (^) is a dead pattern; fix = grep -oE 'pkg==[0-9.]+' or python tomllib; a negative control (fixture with known drift, must exit 1) is mandatory for any gate. Sweep for sibling guards that cannot fail (stale_detector was one).

experiments.title: Evidence Ladder E1-E3: evidence form (anchor -> file fragment -> graph) vs verification quality
experiments.hypothesis: Rung 1 (anchor string) is weak; rung 2 (file fragment) jumps recall; rung 3 (graph) either matches file (structure does not pay off) or beats it on present-trap (structural layer closes the failure mode). One matrix run: 3 models x 3 arms x 50 facts v4_rep.
experiments.command: python scripts/run_1L_live_arm.py --provider openrouter --arm code_first/file_content_first/graph_first --models qwen3.7-flash,deepseek-v4-flash,glm-4.7-flash --prompt-version v2 --no-reasoning --tag 2e_e1/e2/e3; summarize_1L_categories.py --markdown (calls=450, errors=0, ~$0.007)
experiments.result: Rung1->2 confirmed by all 3: qwen recall 0.24->0.92, deepseek 0.04->0.84, glm 0.60->0.68. Rung2->3 non-uniform: qwen graph recall 0.92->0.76 but FA total 0.02->0.000; deepseek graph recall 0.84->0.44 (unknown 0.66 - distrust instead of checking); glm graph recall 0.68->0.84 but FA rises. Reproducibility control: qwen file_content 0.92 vs V4 0.88 (2026-08-15) - inter-run stability confirmed. CORRECTED (RED TEAM on ground truth, 2026-08-15): trap-category numbers of this run are on the mislabeled dataset - real trap-FA = 0 on corrected labels (29T/21F); the file-fragment recall result stands.
experiments.finding: Evidence form is a per-model knob, not a global answer: the file fragment is the strongest recall driver for all models; the graph closes the trap failure mode only for evidence-honest models (and on corrected labels the trap gap itself was a label issue). Fail-open models (glm family) are not cured by ANY evidence form - that is a model property, not an evidence property. CORRECTED (E5, 2026-08-16): on the extended subject-validated trap category (20 false / 10 true) the graph really closes present-trap for deepseek (75%->40%) - the 'graph does not help' reading was an N=1 statistical issue; for glm the graph still does not help (14/20).

chart.title: Recall(real) by evidence rung, %

experiments.conclusion: For VOR: recall engine = file fragment (~25 lines); graph = a separate subject-check signal against traps, but only for evidence-honest models; exclude fail-open models (glm family) from the VOR pipeline.

experiments.title: Evidence Ladder E3b+E4: file+graph hybrid is NOT additive; git-provenance distinguishes existed-then vs exists-now
experiments.hypothesis: (E3b) a file+graph hybrid is additive (file recall + graph trap-zero); (E4) git-provenance (commit+date+branch in evidence) lets models tell 'existed until C' from 'exists at HEAD'.
experiments.command: python scripts/run_1L_live_arm.py --arm file_graph_first (tag 2e_e4) and temporal_first with temporal facts/contexts (tag 2e_e5) - qwen3.7-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, glm-4.7-flash; calls=294, errors=0 (temporal dataset: 48 facts = 12 removed / 28 real / 8 absent, ground truth from git)
experiments.result: HYBRID (v4_rep N=50): qwen acc 0.900 (vs file 0.940 - hybrid is worse than file alone), deepseek FA 0.08 > graph 0.04; glm FA 0.10. TEMPORAL (N=48): deepseek and glm 48/48 (FA=0.00) - 'existed until C' vs 'exists' recognized perfectly on existence-claims; qwen3.7 accepted 5/12 removed (T04/T09-T12, ~42%, Wilson CI 0.19-0.69) - token-level familiarity/noise. CORRECTED: (E3b) 'graph closes trap (1/6->0/6)' was a mislabeled-data issue - R45 is true; the non-additivity result stands. (E4b, 2026-08-16): 'deepseek/glm are temporal-robust, qwen is not' was a prompt-hint issue - WITHOUT the 'NOT FOUND AT HEAD' hint NO model is robust; temporal present-trap is universal, and a past-tense formulation solves it. (E5, 2026-08-16): 'graph does not help against trap' was a N=1 statistical issue - on the extended subject-validated trap category (20 false / 10 true) graph really closes present-trap for deepseek (75%->40%).
experiments.finding: Hybridity is NOT additive: with a file fragment present, token presence dominates and the graph adds nothing (acc 0.900 < file 0.940) - VOR design must pick ONE evidence format: fragment for recall OR graph for trap-precision. Git-provenance is a cheap, powerful temporal signal for 2/3 models on existence-claims but does not cure qwen-family; the 'robust 2/3' framing was itself a hint issue (E4b) - temporal present-trap is universal and formulation solves it. CORRECTED (E5): the trap-precision claim below was measured on a single false fact (R42) - statistically meaningless; on the extended category graph closes trap for deepseek (75->40%) and does not for glm (14/20).

chart.title: Hybrid vs single-format accuracy, %

experiments.conclusion: VOR evidence format is chosen by the target metric: fragment for recall, graph for trap-precision - the hybrid is the worst of both (acc 0.90). Git-provenance in evidence is a cheap temporal signal, but the universal temporal present-trap is solved by claim formulation, not by evidence. CORRECTED (E5): 'graph for trap-precision' is real for deepseek (75->40% on the extended category), not for glm; the N=1 trap measurement that suggested otherwise was a statistical issue.

experiments.title: ONNX embedder down: off-by-one project paths (not the model or ports)
experiments.hypothesis: Fixing PROJECT_ROOT (parent x3 -> parents[3]) in onnx_client/onnx_server restores the ONNX mode: the server finds the script and the model, /embed returns 384-dim.
experiments.command: cd <ext> && PYTHONPATH=<ext> venv/Scripts/python.exe D:/Project/MSCodeBase/.local/onnx_client_check.py; curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9876/embed -d '{"text":"test"}'
experiments.result: [1] ensure_server_running: True; [2] embed status=200; [3] dim=384 first3=[0.037, -0.058, -0.041]; ONNX CLIENT PATH: PASSED. Before the fix: FileNotFoundError 'Model directory not found for: multilingual-e5-small-int8'; server logs: 'failed to load E5-base ONNX' x5/day.
experiments.finding: Root cause is paths, not model/ports: (1) onnx_client looked for '...src/src/core/embedder/onnx_server.py' (duplicated src), (2) onnx_server looked for the model in '.../src/.codebase_models/...' (not the root). The off-by-one was copied between files (onnx_client <- onnx_server).

chart.title: Embed endpoint before/after path fix

experiments.conclusion: Off-by-one paths in src/core/embedder/ are copied between files - when touching paths there, use parents[3] or verify path.exists() on all search_paths; remote_embedder already uses get_extension_dir correctly.

experiments.title: Evidence Ladder E5: extended trap category (N=20, subject-validated labels) - present-trap is mass, graph really helps deepseek (75%->40%)
experiments.hypothesis: 'FA trap = 0' on the v4_rep category rested on a single false fact (R42) - statistically meaningless. With a trap category extended to 20 false / 10 true and labels validated per subject (grep subject = 0), present-trap is measurable and the graph arm's true effect can be estimated.
experiments.command: trap_facts_generator.py (20 false-trap: value in >=2 project files, NOT in the subject file - grep subject=0; 10 true-trap) + file_content_first/graph_first x 3 models (pinned: qwen->Alibaba, deepseek/glm->DeepInfra; first run with Alibaba for all = 404 glm, redone). fp 138f306dbe14b66e -> cb6f822b9eb66afd
experiments.result: FA on 20 real false-trap / recall on 10 true-trap: file_content qwen 2/20, 2/10; deepseek 15/20, 6/10; glm 13/20, 7/10. graph_first qwen 2/20, 3/10; deepseek 8/20, 5/10; glm 14/20, 9/10.
experiments.finding: Present-trap is NOT a mislabel issue: on honest subject-validated labels file_content FA is 2-15/20 (10-75%) - the earlier 'residual trap hole' was distorted by N=1. Graph evidence REALLY closes present-trap for deepseek (75%->40% FA); for glm it does not (14/20); qwen already has low FA (2/20) but pays recall (2-3/10 - fail-closed).

chart.title: False-accept on 20 real present-traps, file vs graph

experiments.conclusion: 'FA trap = 0' on a category with N=1 is a meaningless number; extending the category with subject validation (P-00X) is the only honest way to measure present-trap. Graph evidence is a real trap-closer for deepseek, not for glm - per-model evidence format is confirmed even more strongly.

experiments.title: Pinned-rerun on the corrected dataset (fp e6ce7b90): canonical series numbers, routing band removed
experiments.hypothesis: Unpinned OpenRouter routing (>=8 upstreams, KI-105) adds per-run variance; pinning providers (qwen->Alibaba, deepseek/glm->DeepInfra per the pinned-probe) removes the routing band and gives canonical numbers for the series.
experiments.command: 15 runs (5 arms x 3 models), --pin-provider: qwen->Alibaba, deepseek/glm->DeepInfra (per pinned-probe; StreamLake/Cloudflare-deepseek broken pinned). corrected dataset e6ce7b902d0a20a9 (R44 truth=None). Tags 2e_pin_*. +resume for qwen error-facts. Cost ~$0.02
experiments.result: file_content qwen 0.88/0/3, deepseek 0.80/1/2, glm 0.68/2/1; graph_first qwen 0.72/0/4, deepseek 0.48/0/2, glm 0.84/1/0; file_graph qwen 0.84/0/3, deepseek 0.92/1/2, glm 0.80/2/1 (rec / FA-trap / miss_true). temporal NOW removed-FA: qwen 12/12, deepseek 9/12, glm 12/12; temporal PAST: all 40/40. FA absent/silent: 0 in all pinned cells.
experiments.finding: Routing band removed but per-model conclusions unchanged: file_content is the best recall arm for qwen (0.88), graph for glm (0.84, FA trap 1), hybrid for deepseek (0.92); temporal present-trap is universal (NOW 12/12, 9/12, 12/12), past solved by formulation (40/40). glm stays non-deterministic even pinned (unpin 6FA -> pin-force1 2FA -> pin-force2 1FA) - pinning removed routing, not model variance (+/-0.02-0.04 FA). FA absent/silent = 0 in all pinned evidence arms - the corrected 1-L picture (trap miss_true 4/5 for fail-closed) is routing-independent.

chart.title: Recall(real) per arm, pinned run, %

experiments.conclusion: Pinned-rerun confirmed every series conclusion is robust to routing; glm non-determinism is a model property (even on a single backend); StreamLake (top-1 unpinned for glm) pinned returns no JSON - volume does not equal quality, and pinning also protects against 'popular but broken' upstreams.

negativeResults.attempt: pylint-django as a code duplication detector

x30-65 cost and x20-70 tokens for a marginal recall gain (qwen3.6 code_first 0.08 -> 0.20); glm-4.7 loses 16-26% of responses to upstream EMPTY_CONTENT.
